title: The Real Reason Reading In A Car Makes You Sick
hook: Reading in a car makes your brain think you are poisoned.

narration.text: Reading in a car makes your brain think you are poisoned.
Your eyes see the book, telling your brain you are still.
But your inner ear detects motion, sensing movement.
This mismatch of signals is called sensory conflict.
Your brain interprets this conflict as a sign of toxin exposure.
It then triggers nausea and vomiting to protect you.
This is why looking out the window can help.
Your eyes then see the motion your inner ear feels.
Does looking out the window help you avoid car sickness?

description: Have you ever wondered why reading in a car makes you feel ill? It is all down to a fascinating brain trick called sensory conflict. Your brain gets mixed signals, leading to motion sickness.
topic: Why you get motion sickness when reading in a car, linking it to sensory conflict.
